claims.text: High configurational disorder induces local lattice distortions in the alloy.
Local lattice distortions directly enhance electron–phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling shifts the superconducting critical temperature.
Conventional slow cooling produces moderate, naturally occurring short-range order in the starting alloy.
Rapid quenching increases local lattice distortions relative to slow cooling.
Rapid quenching suppresses emerging short-range order relative to slow cooling.
Greater local lattice distortion will produce broader X-ray diffraction peaks.
Greater local lattice distortion will produce a wider EXAFS bond-length distribution.
Enhanced local lattice distortions alter the alloy's phonon spectrum.
The distortion-induced change in the phonon spectrum increases electron–phonon coupling strength.
Increased electron–phonon coupling enhances the density of states at the Fermi level favorable for superconductivity.
The rapidly quenched alloy will have a higher superconducting transition temperature than the slowly cooled baseline.
The rapidly quenched alloy will exhibit modified electron–phonon coupling characteristics relative to the slowly cooled baseline.
The proposed mechanism is operative only in truly single-phase high-entropy alloys with sufficient configurational entropy.
Magnetic interactions or phase separation may change the proposed distortion–superconductivity relationship.
